The prices moved.

METHODOLOGY

Same quantities, explicit comparison rules

Median represents the middle standardized price in each city's eligible assortment. Fixed cheapest selects the cheapest April product that also exists in November with the same product ID and package quantity, then tracks that exact item.

Standards are: 16 oz apples, tomatoes, butter, ground beef and chicken thighs; 20 oz bread; 15 oz beans; 12 oz broccoli and cereal; 64 fl oz milk; 52 fl oz juice; and 12 eggs.

Category view is independent of the 12-item basket. It uses only exact product-ID matches observed in the same city, search term, and normalized unit on both dates. SKU changes are combined within each term, then terms receive equal weight in the category index. Sample sizes are shown beside every bar.

No product or package substitution is allowed in the fixed basket. April 7 and November 12 were chosen because all four active markets had complete observations on both dates. Ambiguous multipacks and inactive NYC are excluded.
CHEAPEST BASKET · ACTUAL PRODUCTS

Dallas: April vs. November

Every row uses the same product ID and package quantity in both snapshots. Shelf price is the package cost; basket price is the amount attributed to the standardized basket quantity.
CATEGORY INDEX · SUPPORTING PRODUCTS

Dallas Produce: April vs. November

Every row is the same Kroger product ID in April and November, within the same city, search term, and normalized unit. Search terms are grouped so you can audit every SKU contributing to the category index.
